rules.message: FluentValidation.AspNetCore is deprecated (NuGet reason: Legacy), works for MVC only, and runs async rules synchronously.
rules.fix: Reference FluentValidation and FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions 12.x, and call ValidateAsync in an endpoint filter or the action.

rules.message: The FluentValidation.AspNetCore integration is deprecated, does nothing for minimal APIs, and runs async rules synchronously.
rules.fix: Register with AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining<T>() and call ValidateAsync in a generic endpoint filter (references/call-sites.md).

rules.message: A sync Validate call throws AsyncValidatorInvokedSynchronouslyException as soon as the validator has an async rule.
rules.fix: Use await validator.ValidateAsync(model, ct) with the cancellation token.

rules.message: Singleton validators keep each dependency for the life of the app. A scoped dependency (DbContext) becomes a captive dependency.

rules.fix: Use result.ToDictionary() for the messages, and add the error codes as an extension (decision API-20).
match: result.Errors.GroupBy(e => e.PropertyName).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToArray())

result.Errors
    .GroupBy(e => e.PropertyName)
    .ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToArray())
nomatch: result.Errors.GroupBy(e => e.PropertyName).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Select(e => e.ErrorCode).ToArray())

rules.message: A mocked validator hides a missing registration, a sync call, and the error shape.
rules.fix: Test the real validator with TestValidateAsync. Use InlineValidator<T> when a consumer test needs a failing validator.
